summary: Nine labels print willow or white willow bark extract at 400 to 1,600 mg, or willow or bark powder at 200 to 680 mg, and the rows show no salicin. One label carries a joint claim. Every placebo-controlled trial read states its dose as salicin (120 or 240 mg/day), so a label's extract mass can't be matched to a studied dose. For low back pain, 10936472 meets the reading bar on its primary outcome, and Cochrane rates the placebo comparison as moderate quality (25536022). For osteoarthritis the trials conflict (11406860 positive at 2 weeks, 15517622 null at 6 weeks; 19140170 calls this conflicting), and 37895439 pools arthritis trials while calling certainty inadequate. Rheumatoid arthritis was null in 26 patients. Abstracts only.
question_for_clinician: Does the low back pain trial (10936472, 120 and 240 mg salicin/day) and the Cochrane rating (25536022) support credit for willow bark labels that print extract or powder mass with no salicin in the rows? Agent recommendation: no credit, because the studied exposure can't be matched to what these labels print.
